newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Austrian owner not to leave panic-hit Postabank.
newsitem.headline: Austrian owner not to leave panic-hit Postabank.

text.p: Austrian bank Oesterreichische Postsparkasse (OPS) said on Tuesday it did not plan to sell its 10.4 percent stake in Postabank, Hungary's second largest bank, which has been hit by a large wave of withdrawals.
OPS, Postabank's largest foreign owner, said in a news release that it did not see a reason for changing its stake in the bank, Hungarian daily Nepszabadsag said.
A panic run of depositors on Postabank started on Friday as rumours spread that the bank might become insolvent.
OPS said Postabank did not inform it about the tension around the bank and the owner learnt about the panic withdrawals from news agency reports.

However, the results of a banking authority investigation closed late last year and the reassuring words of Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy to depositors showed that the bank was solvent and the panic was not justified, OPS added.
Moody's Investors Service on Monday confirmed the ratings of Postabank for long- and short-term deposits at Ba2 and Not Prime, and its ratings for bank financial strength at D.
Moody's statement added that the withdrawals by Postabank depositors appeared to be rumour-based and were already stabilising.
